title: One Snake Silenced an Island's Forest
subject: brown tree snake

scenes.text: One snake silenced an entire island's forest.
The brown tree snake reached Guam by accident in the 1940s and spread fast.
Guam had 12 native forest bird species. Ten are gone, and the other two are nearly gone.
Why do trees care? About 70 percent of Guam's tree species rely on birds to spread their seeds.
Without birds, around 95 percent of seeds from two common trees fall right beneath the parent, versus under 40 percent on islands that still have birds.
The birds went first. Now the forest itself is slowly stalling.

description:
The brown tree snake reached Guam in the 1940s, and 10 of its 12 native forest bird species are gone.
About 70 percent of its trees rely on birds to spread seeds, so the forest is changing too.
Can a forest survive without its birds?
